notes:
Summary: Quantile is a mid-to-large fintech building a customer-facing conversational assistant + large-scale embeddings catalog for recommender features. Primary ask: dedicated capacity with strict throughput guarantees and predictable unit economics. Baseline requirements from CTO/Infra lead: steady-state 60-90 QPS, peak spikes up to 320-360 QPS for product launches, average response size ~400-600 tokens (tokenized), target 95th percentile end-to-end generation latency <600ms for avg-size conversations. Tokens/sec planning: steady-state ~25k-60k tokens/sec, peak sustained bursts up to ~230k tokens/sec for short windows. They prefer H100-class hardware but are open to mixed fleets (A100/H100 + quantized variants) if Redwood can guarantee latency SLOs. Quote from CTO: "We need a reserve that behaves like a dedicated express lane — predictable throughput and deterministic cost per 1000 tokens."

Workshop outputs and decisions: agreed to run a 2-week POC (hosted) to calibrate kernel/sequence length distribution, followed by an on-prem pilot in one regional datacenter. SE Arjun to produce batch-caching and kv-cache recommendations; recommended autoscale buffer = 25% above measured peak to cover burst headroom. Estimated dedicated footprint: 8-12 H100-equivalent GPUs (final depends on quantization and batching gains) to meet 95p latency <600ms at expected peak QPS with intelligent routing.

SLA negotiation points: explicit throughput guarantees (min baseline QPS), granular latency SLOs at p50/p95/p99, overage handling and burst pricing, network locality/residency clauses, transparent kernel & quantization profile disclosures, scheduled maintenance windows and rollback plan. Procurement wants a 3-year reserved commitment with quarterly performance reviews.
